provider.label: AI provider
provider.desc: Like aside, use your own API key or a local model — you cover the cost with your own key

diag.desc: Checks whether the AI you configured actually works. If not, it tells you the cause and a fix.
diag.requesting: Sending a real request to the current provider…

includePageByDefault.label: Include page content in questions
includePageByDefault.desc: Send the current page body by default (can be toggled off in the sidebar)

memoryEnabled.label: Use memory
memoryEnabled.desc: Reference personal context the AI has saved when answering — no need to re-explain every time (Manage memory)

autoMemory.label: Auto memory extraction (Dreaming)
autoMemory.desc: When a conversation ends, automatically extract memorable facts and save them (off by default — enabling adds an extra request per conversation)

nativeToolUse.label: Agent native function calling
nativeToolUse.desc: On supported models (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Ollama qwen/llama3.1+, etc.) the agent works more reliably via structured function calls. Auto: use it if supported, otherwise fall back to the JSON method

agentVision.label: Agent screen perception (vision)
agentVision.desc: The agent looks at a screenshot of the current screen to decide (helpful for visually complex sites). Auto (recommended) only captures when the screen changes or gets stuck, saving subscription limits and time. Always captures every step (maximum accuracy, higher usage). Supported: Claude, GPT, Gemini (API key), local vision models (llava, llama3.2-vision, etc.), Claude Code (subscription). Automatically off for codex/gemini-cli and plain text models.

triggers.label: AI triggers (automation)
triggers.desc: Automatically runs the agent when entering a site, at a set time each day, or on page-change detection. Persists across restarts. (Open trigger manager)

collectors.label: Daily auto-collect
collectors.desc: Quietly opens specified sites each day, gathers only new items, and sends an AI summary briefing as a notification. (Open collector manager)

profile.label: My info (autofill)
profile.desc: Save your name, address, email, card, etc. safely, and any form gets filled automatically (values are never sent to the AI). (Manage my info)

webhookUrl.label: Collected data webhook
webhookUrl.desc: Sends data collected by the agent to this address as JSON. Connect to Zapier, Make, IFTTT, Google Sheets (Apps Script), Notion, email, etc. Sent via the "🔗 Send" button in the data table.

google.keyHint: Get a free API key: aistudio.google.com → Get API key

claudeCode.title: Claude Code runs via subscription
claudeCode.desc: Runs the agent on your Claude Pro/Max subscription instead of pay-as-you-go API. Install Claude Code locally (claude.com/claude-code), run claude once to log in with your subscription, and this browser will call that CLI. No API key needed.

path.label: Executable path
path.desc: Leave blank to use claude from PATH. Specify a path if needed (e.g. C:\\Users\\me\\AppData\\Roaming\\npm\\claude)

model.label: Model
model.desc: Leave blank for the Claude Code default. To specify, use opus / sonnet / haiku or a full model ID

claudeCode.checkHint: Check: claude --version works in a terminal, and echo hi | claude -p responds — you're ready.

codex.title: Codex runs via ChatGPT subscription
codex.desc: Runs on your ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription instead of pay-as-you-go API. Install Codex CLI locally (npm i -g @openai/codex), run codex and log in with ChatGPT, and this browser will call it via codex exec.

path.label: Executable path
path.desc: Leave blank to use codex from PATH

model.label: Model
model.desc: You must specify a model allowed on your ChatGPT account (varies by account/plan). If left blank, codex's default may be rejected by your account.

codex.checkHint: Check: echo hi | codex exec --skip-git-repo-check - responds — you're ready. If you get a "model is not supported" error, switch to a model your account allows.

geminiCli.title: Gemini CLI Google account
geminiCli.desc: Install Gemini CLI locally (npm i -g @google/gemini-cli), run gemini and log in with your Google account (free tier), and this browser will call it. Runs on your account without an API key.

path.label: Executable path
path.desc: Leave blank to use gemini from PATH

geminiCli.checkHint: Check: gemini --version works and echo hi | gemini responds — you're ready.

ollama.title: Local Ollama
ollama.desc: Install Ollama (ollama.com) and download a model to run fully locally with no API key. e.g. in a terminal: ollama pull llama3.2

model.label: Model
model.desc: Name of an installed model (e.g. llama3.2, qwen2.5)

agentFilesDir.label: Asset folder
agentFilesDir.desc: The folder holding files the agent can upload (including subfolders). Anything outside this folder is blocked. Once set, the agent can upload autonomously — e.g. "post cat.jpg to Instagram" — without a file picker.

agentHumanInput.label: Act like a human (bot-detection avoidance)
agentHumanInput.desc: The agent operates with real mouse movement paths and trusted clicks/keystrokes. Makes it look like a human on bot-detecting sites like Instagram, Facebook, and YouTube (recommended). Turning it off uses faster synthetic events but may get blocked on some sites.

agentInputMode.label: Operation speed
agentInputMode.desc: Human-like timing (mouse paths, keystroke intervals) is needed to avoid bot detection but is slower. Auto (recommended): human speed only on sites known to run bot detection like Instagram/TikTok, and fast real input elsewhere (about 3x faster clicks, 2.5x faster typing). Always human speed: safest but slow. Always fast: fastest but may be detected on some sites.

agentCollapsePanels.label: Auto-collapse panels while running
agentCollapsePanels.desc: While the agent is running, collapses the downloads/video docks and the left side panel to widen the page area, and restores them when done (the AI panel stays). Reduces cases where a large dialog, like Instagram's post window, gets clipped and hides buttons.

cliSession.label: Keep CLI session (Claude Code · Codex)
cliSession.desc: When running the agent via Claude Code or Codex, keeps one CLI process per task and sends steps to it continuously. Removes the boot time and cache loss of relaunching every step, so per-step latency drops a lot and tokens are saved. Turn this off if you run into issues (goes back to relaunching every step).

agentAutoApprove.label: Auto-approve sensitive actions (unattended runs)
agentAutoApprove.desc: By default only actions that spend money or destroy data, like payments, purchases, transfers, or deletions, need confirmation (search, login, form submission, and posting/publishing/uploading proceed without confirmation — so it doesn't get in the way of auto-publishing). Turning this on lets even those risky actions proceed automatically without confirmation. Convenient but risky — only enable it for tasks you trust.

agentMaxSteps.label: Agent max steps
agentMaxSteps.desc: Maximum steps the agent will attempt for one task. Set higher for long tasks like login → upload → publish (default 25, range 6–80)

maxTokens.label: Max response length (tokens)
maxTokens.desc: Max tokens to generate in one reply

maxContextChars.label: Max page context characters
maxContextChars.desc: How many characters of page body to send to the AI

adblock.title: Ad & Tracker Blocking
adblock.applyHint: Changes take effect from the next boot or next page load.

defaultEngine.label: Default search engine
defaultEngine.desc: Used when entering a search query in the address bar

suggestEnabled.label: Autocomplete
suggestEnabled.desc: Show suggestions while typing in the address bar

historyRetention.label: History retention period
historyRetention.desc: Used for address-bar autocomplete and the history page

blockThirdPartyCookies.label: Block third-party cookies
blockThirdPartyCookies.desc: Has a big impact on ads and trackers

passkeyAutoPrompt.label: Auto passkey prompts
passkeyAutoPrompt.desc: Automatic passkey (WebAuthn) requests sites send the moment a page opens. Chrome quietly adds these to the autofill list, but this browser has no such UI, so a Windows "Sign in with a security key" window pops up. Block (default) rejects only that automatic request, while requests the user explicitly triggers by clicking "Sign in with passkey" still go through. Per-site exceptions are in the address bar lock icon.

permissions.title: Site Permissions
permissions.intro: Allow/block camera, microphone, location, notification, and clipboard permissions per site. "Default" follows standard behavior (mostly allow on request). Only sites you've configured are shown here.
permissions.confirmClearAll: Reset permission settings for all sites?

accounts.title: 🔐 Login Accounts
accounts.intro1: With pre-registered IDs and passwords, the agent can get through login screens on its own. Adding an account doesn't turn this on automatically — it only works when you explicitly enable "Allow auto-login" per account.
accounts.intro2: CAPTCHAs and verification codes (2FA) are not handled automatically — those are handed off to you.

askEveryTime.desc: Show a dialog when a download starts

ytdlpAutoUpdate.desc: YouTube etc. change often, so staying up to date matters — checked once a day
